\altyazi{fig:study_overview}{\textbf{Study overview as one scene.} (a) Trained models: the two-by-two design, one slice per run, beside the R32 bridge; (b) Reference panels, decks of robust CNNs, sliced into (c) their PGD-10 matrices; (d) Registered before measurement gives the test families; (e) Exact split and contrasts factors each log rate. Depth runs from inputs (back) to the derived split (front).}  % 59 words
\altyazi{fig:design_recipe}{\textbf{Architecture-by-initialization design as a card cabinet.} On CIFAR-10 the drawer rows ViT-Tiny and ResNet-18 cross the columns scratch (random init.) and ImageNet init.; each drawer gives its clean stage (epochs, learning rate) and seeds, one index card per run. The R32 bridge drawer keeps its own recipe; the sign on top is the AT recipe of the four cells.}  % 59 words
\altyazi{fig:decomposition_schematic}{\textbf{Decomposition used throughout, in three tiers.} Top to bottom, the arrows per pair (i, j), panel mean and R minus V mark three steps: the log transfer rate splits exactly into vulnerability, similarity and half a directional residual; panel averages give $\sigma$ and $\rho$; the source gap G splits into symmetric and directional parts. Tiers recede with the aggregation level.}  % 60 words
\altyazi{fig:panel_members}{\textbf{Reference panel members on two catalogue cards.} The upper card, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, gives each RobustBench identifier its role in the C10 and C100 columns and marks ResNet-18 variants in the R18 column. The lower card, ImageNetV2, holds the CNN panel and the secondary XCiT-S12, the transformer pairs and the unpaired ViT-B of Mo et al.}  % 56 words
\altyazi{fig:registry_map}{\textbf{Registered tests and decision rules.} Each band is one family, numbered in registration order and grouped into the main registration and the addendum; rows give test and quantity, place the predicted size (diamond) and falsification threshold (circle) on a number line with the $\pm$0.1 band, and state the falsifying rule. Holm correction is per family; ImageNetV2 rows are descriptive.}  % 59 words
\altyazi{fig:prereg_chain}{\textbf{Pre-registration chain.} Seen beforehand lists the data looked at before registration; Main registration: B2-B6 and Supplement: B8-B10, the addendum of the text, give each block's models, images and cells. Time runs left to right; arrows carry the freeze dates (October 2026), commits and registration digest prefix; the strip Added after the fact names two post hoc analyses.}  % 57 words
\altyazi{fig:source_gap_split}{\textbf{Source gap split into symmetric and directional parts.} One card per data set, one log-unit scale; per seed pair on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 and per same-recipe pair on ImageNetV2 (descriptive): olive symmetric part, lavender-grey directional part, diamond total G; each row prints G and the share q. A dashed part narrows the gap.}  % 53 words
\altyazi{fig:similarity_matrix}{\textbf{Pairwise symmetric similarity.} $\log\simt$ (split-half) for all models on CIFAR-10 (1), CIFAR-100 (2) and ImageNetV2 (3), rows and columns in frozen group order; cell colour is one of five pooled quintile bins with rounded bins, the dark diagonal undefined, dark frames mark the groups. Scratch-trained ViT-Tiny seeds form a block dissimilar to the CNN panel.}  % 56 words
\altyazi{fig:cells_interaction}{\textbf{Two-by-two cells on CIFAR-10.} Panels Panel similarity $\sigma$, Direction $\rho$ and Vulnerability $\omega$ share the initialization positions scratch and ImageNet; lines join cell means (split-half, log scale), open marks are runs, diamonds the R32 bridge. $\sigma$ prints $\Asig{scr}$ (H1) and $\Isig$ (H2); $\rho$ carries the $\pm$0.10 band. Each panel has its own scale.}  % 54 words
\altyazi{fig:attack_side}{\textbf{Transfer by attack, per source.} Each row is one source model, grouped by cell; marks sit at its panel-mean log transfer L(m) under PGD-10 (circle), momentum PGD (square) and, for ViT sources, TGR (triangle). Filled marks are the attacks chosen by cross-fitted selection; TGR is never chosen.}  % 47 words
\altyazi{fig:gradient_alignment}{\textbf{Input-gradient alignment against similarity.} Cosine c between input gradients against $\log\simt$ for every model pair on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNetV2; upper panels raw, lower panels residual, after the additive model main effects are removed from both matrices. Each panel prints the Spearman r and pair count n.}  % 48 words
\altyazi{fig:estimates_forest}{\textbf{Registered estimates.} Upper panel, Contrasts on panel similarity $\sigma$: H1, H2 and descriptive ImageNetV2 rows; lower panel, Directional terms: K-b and H3. Circles log, diamonds logit, open marks descriptive; thick and thin bars are 90\% and 95\% intervals; the $\pm$0.10 lines apply to log rows only.}  % 46 words
\altyazi{fig:protocol_settings}{\textbf{Protocol by setting.} Transfer asymmetry (CNN to ViT minus ViT to CNN) on one shared scale: panels 1-4 are the conditioning protocols; rows are settings, mean$\pm$SD over three seed pairs, pairs as small circles (SVHN two, no mean). The narrow panel at the right prints the spread over the four protocols.}  % 51 words
\altyazi{fig:protocol_sets}{\textbf{Conditioning sets and measured asymmetry.} Conditioning sets: nested evaluation sets as terraces (schematic, not area-proportional; terrace height carries no value) with masks and mean N. Measured asymmetry: mean$\pm$SD of the within-pair difference, pairs as open circles, mean$\pm$SD printed per row; the steps print the three decomposition terms.}  % 47 words
\altyazi{fig:spread_clean_gap}{\textbf{Protocol spread against the clean-accuracy gap, all 60 model pairs.} Upper panel, Three-protocol spread: unconditioned, target-correct and both-correct, rings the identity prediction at p = 1; lower panel, Successful-source minus both-correct, the term the spread leaves out. No line is fitted.}  % 41 words
\altyazi{fig:epsilon_sweep}{\textbf{Robust accuracy under PGD-10.} CIFAR-10 test accuracy over the budget $\eps$, clean to 16/255, for ViT-Tiny AT, ResNet-18 AT and WRN-28-10; the number rows under the chart print the plotted values (mean of three seed pairs; WRN-28-10 is one RobustBench model).}  % 41 words
\altyazi{fig:feature_degradation}{\textbf{Feature degradation of ViT-Tiny under attack, block by block.} Clean and PGD-10 images enter the stack, block 1 at the bottom; three cards per block, three runs: Entropy $\Delta$, CLS attention entropy change with 90\% TOST intervals, $\pm$0.05-nat band; TV, attention displacement, mean$\pm$SD; Cosine, clean-to-adversarial cosine of CLS token, patch mean and all tokens.
